title.narrative: Emergency Cash for Food Assistance - SAD

description.narrative:
This project seeks to deliver life-saving emergency cash assistance for food security to drought-affected households in Bardera District, Gedo Region, Jubaland State, Somalia. The intervention is designed in response to worsening humanitarian conditions caused byprolonged rainfall failure, climate variability, and recurring environmental shocks that have severely disrupted agricultural production, livestock systems, and income-generating opportunities. As a result, vulnerable households—particularly internally displaced persons (IDPs) and agro-pastoral communities—are facing acute food insecurity, with many falling under IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) and Phase 4 (Emergency).Food access in Bardera is constrained not by market availability but by a critical lack of purchasing power. Despitelocal markets remaining functional and stocked, nearly 80% of households rely on humanitarian assistance and report consuming only one meal per day, significantly below minimum dietary requirements. This has heightened risks ofacute malnutrition, particularly among children, pregnant and lactating women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.
To address these urgent needs, the project will provide unconditional cash transfers to 250 highly vulnerable households (approximately 1,500 individuals) across three IDP camps—Jirix, Hogol, and Tugerey—over a two-month period (March–April 2026). Each household will receive USD 80 per cycle through secure mobile money platforms, aligned with the regional Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) to support access to essential food commodities such as cereals, pulses, oil, and sugar.The intervention will be implemented by Oxfam in partnership with the Social Life and Agricultural Development Organization (SADO), a well-established local NGO with over three decades of experience delivering integrated humanitarian and resilience programming. SADO’s strong community presence and established relationships with local authorities and communities will ensure timely, context-sensitive, and accountable delivery of assistance.
The project adopts a cash-for-food approach, recognizing that cash-based responses are the most appropriate and efficient modality in contexts where markets are functional. Thisapproach promotes dignity, flexibility, and household choice, allowing beneficiaries to prioritize their most urgent needs while also stimulating local market systems.Key activities will include community mobilization and sensitization, participatory beneficiary targeting using vulnerability criteria, cash disbursement through mobile money, real-time distribution monitoring, and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) to assess utilization and impact.
The project will also establish robust accountability mechanisms, includingcommunity feedback channels, complaint systems, and help desks, to ensure transparency and responsiveness to beneficiary concerns. In addition, basic awareness sessions on food consumption and nutrition will be conducted to enhance the effective use of cash assistance.The intervention prioritizes the most vulnerable groups, including female-headed households, households with malnourished children, elderly-headed households, persons with disabilities, and households with limited or no income sources. By targeting these groups, theproject aims to ensure equitable access to assistance and reduce protection risks associated with food insecurity.Expected outcomes include improved household food consumption, restored purchasing power, reduced reliance on negative coping strategies such as borrowing or skipping meals, and enhanced dignity and well-being among beneficiaries. The project will also contribute to stabilizing local markets and strengthening community resilience in the face of ongoing climatic shocks.With a total budget of €46,000, this intervention represents a timely, cost-effective, and scalable response to prevent further deterioration of food security and nutrition outcomes in Bardera District. By addressing immediate food needs while reinforcing local systems, the project aligns with bestpractices in humanitarian cash programming and supports both immediate relief and short-term recovery for drought-affected populations.

participating-org.narrative: Social Life and Agricultural Development Organization (SADO) is a Somalia based Local Non-Governmental Organization (LNGO) established in 1994 with the aim of spearheading local development initiatives in GEDO region and other parts of South-Central Somalia. SADOis legally registered in Kenya and in Somalia under Somalia Federal Government and in Jubaland State of Somalia. With its headquarters in Mogadishu, Somalia, SADO has base stations in Kismayu, Bardera, Elwak, Garbaharrey, Belt Hawa and Dollow Districts of Somalia. It has operational presence and experience in the greater Horn of Africa. SADO is a firm believer in the fundamental moral principle of humanity; that all human begins are born free and equal in dignity and rights and therefore action should be taken to prevent or alleviate human suffering arising out of disaster or conflict, and that nothing should override this principle. Our activities are grounded on the rights-based approach on the belief that people are entitled to basic conditions of living with dignity and have access to equal opportunity as a basis of fulfilling their human potential. MISSION Our mission is to work with our partners in improving the quality of life of vulnerable communities in Somalia through facilitating humanitarian aid and sustainable development programs. A horn of Africa in which vulnerable communities live in dignity and security. CORE VALUES SADO believes in, and is guided by the following ideals: respect, moral and ethical standards, making sound judgments in our programming and innovations.
